subject.title: Incomplete turn with tool call and payloads=0 is replayUnsafe and may poison session state

question: Should replay-unsafe empty stop turns with pending or configured tool activity be retried/fallback-eligible, quarantined with a durable repair record, or kept terminal with stronger diagnostics?
rationale: Current code intentionally treats replay-unsafe attempts as no-retry to avoid duplicating side effects, but field evidence shows that policy causes recurring hard cron failures and may leave malformed session state behind.

options.title: Approve current-attempt retry plus quarantine
options.body: Retry or fall back only when the failed current attempt has no committed side effects, and persist/log a quarantine or repair record for the unsafe terminal attempt.

options.title: Diagnostics-only for now
options.body: Keep replay-unsafe empty turns terminal but add structured incident logs and session-state inspection so maintainers can prove the poisoning path before changing retry behavior.

options.title: Keep fail-closed unchanged
options.body: Accept the current safety boundary and document model/provider workarounds for this signature, leaving recovery to provider choice or manual intervention.

recommendation.title: Approve current-attempt retry plus quarantine
recommendation.body: Retry or fall back only when the failed current attempt has no committed side effects, and persist/log a quarantine or repair record for the unsafe terminal attempt.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant commits and tests show recent hands-on work around the same replay-safety boundary, and the remaining choice is a product/runtime safety policy decision.
